themes.name: Pechersk and Lypky in Kyiv, Ukraine: 1900s brick tenements of four to seven storeys in pastel stucco, ornate eclectic facades on Lutheranska, Zankovetska and Horodetskoho streets
Khreshchatyk street in Kyiv, Ukraine: 1950s Stalinist empire facades of ochre ceramic tiles with arcades, pilasters and heavy cornices, seven to ten storeys
Hrushevskoho street in Kyiv, Ukraine: 1930s Stalinist government blocks of grey stone, the classical Parliamentary library, the Philharmonic
the Dnipro slopes parks of Kyiv, Ukraine: chestnut and linden trees, cast-iron lamps, a few park pavilions, a glass office
Kyiv city centre, Ukraine: Stalinist pale stone blocks on Khreshchatyk, golden-domed churches, Soviet panel blocks
Chernihiv region and Polissia, Ukraine: wooden village houses with carved window frames, white khaty, pine and birch forest, Chernihiv medieval white churches
Sumy and Kharkiv, Slobozhanshchyna, Ukraine: red-brick merchant houses, Kharkiv constructivist concrete, wide avenues, poplars
Kharkiv city, Ukraine: famously clean, well-kept streets with many benches, litter bins, flower beds and neat lawns; Poltavskyi Shliakh, Universytetska street, Constitution square

themes.name: Donbas, Ukraine: mine headframes, slag heaps, brick factory halls with chimneys, workers' barracks, apricot trees
Mariupol and the Azov coast, Ukraine: steelworks, seafront, whitewashed fishing houses, acacia
the Tavria and Crimean steppe, Ukraine: flat fields of sunflowers and wheat, grain elevators, single-storey houses with grape pergolas, poplar windbreaks
Kerch and eastern Crimea, Ukraine: limestone houses, dry hills, the Kerch strait, Genoese towers, cypress
the South Coast of Crimea, Ukraine: Yalta villas and sanatoria with balconies, palms and cypresses, Sevastopol white colonnades
the Dnipro steppe: north Crimea, Melitopol, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Ukraine: irrigation canals, Soviet avenues, Kherson merchant houses, watermelon fields
Odesa and the Black Sea coast, Ukraine: Italianate neoclassical facades with stucco and balconies, courtyards, acacias, limestone
Bessarabia and the Danube, Ukraine: Izmail, reeds and lakes, blue-painted village houses, vineyards

Podillia and the Dnister valley in Ukraine: the port of Odesa left behind, rolling black-earth farmland, Vinnytsia town houses of brick and stucco, the old stone fortress town of Kamianets-Podilskyi on river cliffs
Chernivtsi and Bukovyna, Ukraine: Austro-Hungarian secession facades in ochre and green, rolling hills, orchards
the Carpathians and Zakarpattia, Ukraine: wooden churches with shingle roofs, steep-roofed mountain houses, spruce forest
Halychyna and Volyn, Ukraine: Lviv Renaissance and Baroque townhouses, Lutsk castle, Volyn villages, pine
